messages:
anya: Hey team — OpaqueDelta asked for a concise multi-SLA perf run. They want: 1) sustained 100 qps for chat (seq ~512), 2) spike bursts to 800 qps for short periods, and 3) an SLO matrix for 95/99/99.9 latencies across two model configs (redwood-7B float32 and redwood-7B-4bit). Can we confirm a run plan and ballpark cost?

sam (SRE): +1. I sketched a plan. Short version: warm 15m, steady-state 30m @100 qps, then 10x burst steps (200/400/800 qps) for 2m each, cooldown 10m. Measure p95/p99/p99.9, CPU/GPU util, KV cache hit ratio. Use header tag x-customer:opaquedelta.

lucy (SE): Do we need Dedicated for the 800 qps bursts to keep tail reasonable? OpaqueDelta cares about tail latency at scale; they mentioned 250ms p95 target for chat.

ben (Solutions Eng): Likely need Dedicated or at least reserved burst capacity. Quick estimate: for redwood-7B float32 expect ~3x token cost vs 4-bit. For 100 qps steady with avg output 60 tok/resp, rough token rate = 6000 tok/s => ~518M tokens per day — pricing depends on their committed tier. I'll give a sample calc after plan confirmed.

sam (SRE): Notes on config:
```
- models: [redwood-7b, redwood-7b-4bit]
- seq_in: 128 (prompt), seq_out: 384 (avg) => 512 total
- qps_profile: [steady:100, bursts:200,400,800]
- batching: target batch_size 8 for 4bit, 16 for fp32 where possible
- warmup: prefix cache populate with 5k sample prompts
- metrics: per-route token/sec, gpu_util, request_latency_histogram, dropped_reqs
```

anya: Nice. Can you add the exact ci commands we should run so SD can reproduce? Customer wants reproducible artifacts.

sam (SRE): Sure. Example run command for our bench harness: 
```bash
./bench/run_bench.sh \
  --model redwood-7b-4bit \
  --profile ../profiles/opaquedelta_multi_sla.json \
  --duration 3200s \
  --out results/opaquedelta-7b-4bit.json \
  --tags "customer:opaquedelta,trial:multi-sla"
```
Profile contains the qps steps and payload distributions. I'll drop the profile to the shared drive after this thread.

lucy (SE): For the price calc: please give per-hour GPU estimate and token estimate for both configs. Also note KMS/HSM if they enable encryption at rest — that might add ops overhead.

ben (Solutions Eng): Quick ballpark: on our hosted list-rate, 7B fp32 ~ $1.25/hr per instance (serving slices), 7B-4bit ~ $0.45/hr. For dedicated pricing we discount on commit. For the test run (6h total including warm/cool), hosted run cost ~ (fp32 instances * hr) + bandwidth. But the dominant is token compute: assume 0.0000009 $/token for fp32 (example) and 0.00000035 $/token for 4bit. I'll make a spreadsheet.

anya: OpaqueDelta also sent a security questionnaire about egress and data retention; Security flagged that we need to state whether logs contain PII and whether we can redact. Can engineering confirm how we handle prompt storage during bench runs?

sam (SRE): Bench harness logs full prompts by default for debugging. For customer-facing runs we have a redact flag: `--redact-prompts` which hashes inputs and stores only hashes + token counts. Recommend using redact for PII-sensitive runs and provide them the redaction proof.

ben (Solutions Eng): Also note: when using Dedicated, data never leaves their VPC if they pick Private deployment, but our hosted bench uses temporary storage in a secure bucket. We can provide a signed access window for auditors.

anya: Cool. OpaqueDelta asked about run artifacts: they want a short summary with heatmaps, cost delta between configs, and a recommendation. Can someone own the results writeup?

lucy (SE): I can draft the writeup once we have results. Template: one-pager with TL;DR, test config, steady/burst graphs (qps vs latency), p95/p99/p99.9 table, GPU util chart, cost appendix, recommendation.

sam (SRE): I'll run the bench tonight. Plan: start 02:00 UTC, expected end 08:00 UTC. I'll push profiles and the raw results to gs://redwood-temp/opaquedelta/ and ping here with links.

deploy-bot: deploy started for bench-run-v3 at 02:00 UTC — tracking id bench-opaquedelta-2024-06-12.

ben (Solutions Eng): One more ops note — if we see tail spikes at 800 qps on hosted, immediate fallback is to route bursts to a cheaper 4bit variant with a short-circuit policy and add a 95th percentile SLA notice. Suggest enabling automatic fallback in routing policy for the test.

anya: Approved. Also mark action items: 1) sam run and upload artifacts, 2) lucy draft writeup, 3) ben finalize cost sheet, 4) anya prepare short deck for customer.

sam (SRE): Running now. I'll post a quick interim check after steady-state finishes.

sam (SRE): interim: steady-state 100 qps done for 30m on 7b-4bit. p95 ~ 120ms, p99 ~ 280ms, p99.9 ~ 520ms. GPU util 62%, batch size ~8. No dropped reqs. Uploading partial results: https://storage.redwood/example/opaquedelta/partial-7b-4bit.json

lucy (SE): those tail numbers look good for 4bit. Can we get same for fp32?

sam (SRE): Next run queued for fp32, will follow same schedule.

ben (Solutions Eng): From interim: 4bit meets their p95 target easily. If fp32 has higher batch efficiency maybe tail tighter at high burst but cost 3x. We'll quantify in the sheet.

anya: Great — keep me posted. Customer meeting Friday EOD; need writeup by Friday noon PST.

lucy (SE): Noted. I'll prep the one-pager template now and drop it into the shared drive so I can fill in once sam uploads final results.

sam (SRE): final: completed all runs. Summary quick numbers attached in results summary (gs://redwood-temp/opaquedelta/final-summary.json). Topline: 4bit: steady p95 125ms, burst@800 p95 450ms, burst@800 p99.9 1.2s. fp32: steady p95 95ms, burst@800 p95 230ms, burst@800 p99.9 650ms. Cost delta: ~3.1x per-token cost fp32 vs 4bit.

ben (Solutions Eng): Recommendation: For production w/ strict tail requirements pick fp32 on Dedicated for primary traffic and enable 4bit variant for cost-efficient bulk where occasional tail degradation is tolerable. If they prefer single-tier, tune autoscale to favor more slices during predictable spikes.

anya: Perfect. Lucy — can you finalize the writeup & deck? Ben — finalize cost appendix and SLA bullets. Sam — please include the redact proof and the run profile.

lucy (SE): Will do. Target to post final doc by 16:00 PST today. Link to draft: https://docs.redwood/opaquedelta/perf-writeup-draft

ben (Solutions Eng): I'll attach the cost spreadsheet and a short pricing note for enterprise commit tiers.

anya: Thanks everyone. I'll sync with OpaqueDelta after deck is ready. :thumbsup:

sam (SRE): all artifacts uploaded and permissions set. Closing thread once doc is finalized.

deploy-bot: bench run bench-opaquedelta-2024-06-12 completed — status: success.
